outcomes: A new contributor can move from workspace discovery to an exact validation command and then to focused diagnostics using only public guidance
Generated assistant guidance and public CLI documentation describe the same commands, selection rules, MCP routing, support promise, and failure workflow
Repository contributors use the workspace wrapper for build, test, lint, dependency, and generation workflows
nonGoals: Publishing the internal cli-model module or adding it to the public support catalog
Claiming Python is default, production-ready, or at parity with Go and TypeScript
Announcing a release, changing the current license, or promising pre-1.0 minor compatibility

requirements.text: Top-level, command, Markdown, man-page, completion, and structured help are derived from the command catalog and cover every public command.
Public guidance presents workspace and project discovery, feature and specification discovery, project selection, plan preview, the validation gate, and diagnostic recall as one usable path.

Generated context routes structural discovery to live lock-resolved MCP instructions and resources, names the CLI gate for verification, and states the bounded local fallback when MCP data is unavailable or stale.
Documentation identifies the CLI package as stable under the pre-1.0 migration policy while keeping feature maturity dependent on generated evidence.
Documentation identifies cli-model as an unpublished internal companion that depends only on protocol modules and is tested through the workspace wrapper.
Canonical guidance describes Python as experimental, explicit opt-in, non-default, and without Go or TypeScript parity.
